hi, 

some time ago i started a topic on the beginners section named "TEA and my milky films"

i dont know if you remember

the problem was nomatter how carefully i treated m films with TEA the outcome was always a foggy film.

So if you looked through the film, there was a hologram with a colourshift but it looked as if someone had spilled milk over it. 

It took me an awful lot of time to figure out the problem. 

**Now I know.** The TEA itself was the problem, it must have been poluted or just chemistry of bad quality.

Its now almost a year ago since I ordered one liter of TEA from phtographers formulary. 

Back then i did not know that it was available in Germany aswell, so I ordered it in the US. Because I didnt want to order a new bottle every few month (and pay those enormous shipping costs again and again) I thaught the one liter bottle would be enough TEA for the rest of my life.

Last month I ordered a small bottle of TEA from a germany supplyer (they get their chemestry from sigma aldrich)

and since the i get the cleanest and most colourful holograms ever.

So here my advice, dont det your TEA from photographers formulary.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Interesting! My TEA has always come from Photographer's Formulary and I noticed that my milky haze was cured by carefully damp-wiping and cleaning the non-emulsion side of the plate before exposure. Apparently the dried TEA solution left a kind of oily looking residue on the glass side of the plate that was not at all obvious until it became part of a hologram. The scum is most easily viewed by reflection from a distant safelight. It could be impurities, or more likely the TEA itself is responsible for this - I mean when you remove water from a syrupy liquid film it is unlikely to dry optically clear. If you have found a variety of TEA that dries cleanly without wiping and polishing, that would be great!

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: OK, understand now. I haven't had problems myself, but since you see a clear difference with purer TEA I wonder what's going on chemically. Maybe the impurities were interacting with your developer somehow? I use Metol/Ascorbic acid developer nowadays which doesn't seem to be sensitive to this. I have also tried rinsing out the TEA before developing, but didn't notice any difference in results.
